### Problem 1
#### Dataset Description
```{r load-noaa}
data("ny_noaa")

dim(ny_noaa)
names(ny_noaa)
summary(ny_noaa)
```
The `ny_noaa` dataset contains `r nrow(ny_noaa)` observations and `r ncol(ny_noaa)` variables from `r n_distinct(ny_noaa$id)` weather stations in New York State. The observations span from `r min(ny_noaa$date)` to `r max(ny_noaa$date)`. Key variables include station ID (`id`), date (`date`), precipitation (`prcp`), snowfall (`snow`), snow depth (`snwd`), maximum temperature (`tmax`), and minimum temperature (`tmin`).

Missing data are present in several variables, including `r sum(is.na(ny_noaa$prcp))` missing values for precipitation, `r sum(is.na(ny_noaa$snow))` for snowfall, `r sum(is.na(ny_noaa$snwd))` for snow depth, `r sum(is.na(ny_noaa$tmax))` for maximum temperature, and `r sum(is.na(ny_noaa$tmin))` for minimum temperature. In addition, `tmax` and `tmin` are currently stored as character variables and will need to be converted during data cleaning.

#### Data Cleaning and Snowfall
```{r clean-noaa}
ny_noaa =
  ny_noaa |>
  mutate(
    year = year(date),
    month = month(date),
    day = day(date),
    prcp = prcp / 10,
    snow = snow,
    snwd = snwd,
    tmax = as.numeric(tmax) / 10,
    tmin = as.numeric(tmin) / 10
  )
```

```{r snowfall-frequency}
ny_noaa |>
  filter(!is.na(snow)) |>
  count(snow, sort = TRUE) |>
  head(10)
```

The most commonly observed snowfall value is `r ny_noaa |> filter(!is.na(snow)) |> count(snow, sort = TRUE) |> slice(1) |> pull(snow)` mm. Other common snowfall values include `r ny_noaa |> filter(!is.na(snow)) |> count(snow, sort = TRUE) |> slice(2:5) |> pull(snow) |> paste(collapse = ", ")` mm. The large number of 0 mm observations is expected because snowfall does not occur on most station-days. The repeated nonzero values likely reflect commonly reported snowfall amounts and rounding in the measurement process.

#### Average Maximum Temperature in January and July

```{r}
temp_month_df =
  ny_noaa |>
  filter(month %in% c(1, 7)) |>
  group_by(id, year, month) |>
  summarize(
    mean_tmax = mean(tmax, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) |>
  filter(!is.nan(mean_tmax)) |>
  mutate(
    month = factor(
      month,
      levels = c(1, 7),
      labels = c("January", "July")
    )
  )
```

```{r}
temp_month_df |>
  ggplot(aes(x = year, y = mean_tmax, group = id)) +
  geom_line(alpha = 0.2) +
  facet_grid(. ~ month) +
  labs(
    title = "Average Maximum Temperature in January and July",
    x = "Year",
    y = "Average maximum temperature (°C)"
  )
```

January temperatures are much lower and more variable than July temperatures. The mean January maximum temperature is `r temp_month_df |> filter(month == "January") |> summarize(mean(mean_tmax, na.rm = TRUE)) |> pull() |> round(1)` °C, compared with `r temp_month_df |> filter(month == "July") |> summarize(mean(mean_tmax, na.rm = TRUE)) |> pull() |> round(1)` °C in July. Both months show clear year-to-year variation across stations, but July temperatures are more tightly clustered. A few unusually low station-year averages appear to be potential outliers, especially in January.
